subject: baku
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: baku, the dream-eating tapir spirit.
Style: ukiyo-e woodblock print.

spec.name: Baku, the Dream-Eating Tapir Spirit
spec.description: A Malayan-tapir-bodied baku with an elephant trunk, a fierce gold-eyed face, a tiger-pawed stance and an ox tail, drawn as an ukiyo-e woodblock print: indigo and cream saddle, seigaiha waves, vermilion and gold flame mane, and a dream-cloud wisp drifting into its trunk.
spec.layout: Side-on quadruped facing +Z, centred on x=0. Body: a heavy barrel torso (belly at y~0.62, back at y~1.4) from the haunches at z=-1.1 to the chest at z=0.95. Tapir colouring as a woodblock print: indigo head, neck, shoulders, forelegs, hindquarters, hindlegs and tail; a creamy saddle band over back, flanks and belly from z=+0.35 back to z=-0.5. The saddle edge is a scalloped line. A sumi-black outline stroke runs along the spine and the saddle edge. The saddle carries seigaiha (overlapping concentric wave arcs) in pale blue and indigo as small flat parts seated on the surface. The neck rises from z=0.8 into a long wedge head with a domed forehead. Tiny fierce rhino-style eyes have gold irises, sumi pupils and vermilion brows. Vermilion kabuki-style cheek lines and a tomoe mark sit on the forehead. Round ears have cream rims and tips. Short ivory tusks flank the trunk root. The trunk droops forward and down to a tip at y~0.9, z~1.8, with cream wrinkle rings and pink nostrils. A dream-cloud wisp (sumi-outlined lilac and grey-blue scrolls, a small glowing moon, tiny stars) curls into the trunk tip. Four sturdy legs end in tiger paws with ivory claws, vermilion cuff bands and cream fur tufts; the paws rest on y=0. A crest of overlapping flame-shaped blades runs from the nape along the back to the rump, shaded vermilion, then gold, then cream at the tips, with sumi edges. Kumo (cloud scroll) roundels in vermilion and gold sit on shoulders and haunches. The ox tail curls up in an S and ends in a flame tuft in the same palette. Style on every part: flat colours only, bold sumi outlines as thin dark sweeps and rims, hard colour bands (bokashi done as 2-3 stepped tones), no smooth gradients, chunky simplified shapes. Facets stay low-poly. Left is +X.

parts.builds: The torso, one smooth loft on the pelvis/spine1/chest bones, from the rump at z=-1.1 to the chest at z=0.95. Half-width ~0.45, belly at y~0.62, back at y~1.4, with a high rounded rump and a deep chest. Tapir colouring through bands and sectors: indigo at the chest and shoulders (z>0.35) and the hindquarters (z<-0.5), cream saddle between over back, flanks and belly. The saddle edges are scalloped by rows of small indigo and cream wedge or disc parts seated on the surface (a woodblock zig-zag), not smooth lines. Seigaiha wave motif on the saddle flanks: rows of stacked small flat discs (cream, waveBlue, indigo, cream, shrinking) overlapped in a scale pattern, about 3 rows by 6 on each flank, plus a few on the back. A thin sumi stroke (thin sweep along the surface) edges the saddle front and rear and runs down the spine. Belly shadow band in indigoLight under the cream. A vermilion sash or belly cord with a gold knot and two ivory tassel strands hangs on the left flank of the saddle (a Shinto-spirit rope), a small gold bell at the knot. Rump: two sumi swirl lines on each haunch, hip bone bumps in indigoLight. Everything is flat-coloured with sumi outlines on the main silhouette edges.
parts.attaches: Neck tube starts at neckBase on the chest's front top. Legs hang from shoulderL/R and hipL/R (the leg tops sit inside the torso). The crest and tail start on the back at napeCrest..backCrestEnd and tailRoot at the rump.

parts.builds: Neck and head. A thick indigo neck sweep on neck1/neck2 from neckBase to headBase (radius ~0.2 tapering to 0.17), with a cream chest-bib scallop line and a sumi outline. Skull: a long wedge head, domed forehead, tapering muzzle toward trunkRoot (z up to 1.52), half-width ~0.18, indigo with an indigoLight highlight on the brow. Separate lower jaw on the jaw joint (indigo, cream chin), with an open-able mouth line in sumi, a beniPink tongue and small ivory teeth seated at the lip line. Rhino-style small, fierce eyes at about (±0.16, 1.42, 1.3): sumi almond outline, gold iris disc, black slit pupil, white glint dot; vermilion angled brow bars above each eye with a sumi underline. Kabuki-style kumadori cheek lines in vermilion (three sweeping lines per cheek), a vermilion tomoe (comma-swirl, built from two small spiral sweeps and a disc) on the forehead with a gold ring. Two short curved ivory tusks at the trunk root (±0.09, 1.2, 1.5) pointing down and forward. Round ears on earL/earR: indigo discs, cream rims, beniPink inner discs, cream tips, with a sumi outline ring, tilted outward and back. Long whisker strands (thin sumi sweeps) at the muzzle sides, and a few sumi hair strokes on the cheeks and forehead. Everything is flat-coloured, with bold outlines, no gradients.
parts.attaches: The neck starts at neckBase on the body chest. The trunk part begins at trunkRoot (z~1.5) at the muzzle front, so leave the front face of the muzzle open there. The mane crest starts at napeCrest behind the skull.

parts.builds: The elephant-like trunk and the dream it eats. The trunk is a tapering smooth sweep on trunk1..trunk3 from trunkRoot (radius ~0.11) drooping forward and down to trunkTip (radius ~0.065), indigo on top and cream-grey underneath (sectors), with 7-8 thin cream wrinkle rings (ring or along parts), a sumi outline stroke along the top, and a vermilion lip ridge on the upper trunk near the root. The tip is slightly flared, with two sumi nostril holes ringed in beniPink and a small finger-like lip. The dream: a wisp rolling in from the front side of the tip and drawn into the nostrils, built as 3-4 layered kumo cloud scrolls (spiral sweeps and stacked disc clusters), cloudGrey and dreamLilac with paper highlights and sumi outlines, each cloud a flat-coloured bundle of round puffs; a small glowing moonGlow moon (sphere with a sumi crescent shadow disc) and 4-6 tiny starWhite glowing stars (use the glow kit) sit inside the cloud. A thin dream-thread ribbon (a sweep in dreamLilac) spirals from the cloud into the nostril. The wisp stays beside and in front of the trunk tip and never covers the face.
parts.attaches: Root meets the muzzle at trunkRoot. The dream ribbon ends at trunkTip / dreamMouth.

parts.builds: Four legs, each a smooth sweep on its own leg chain (front: shoulderFL/FR to elbow, wrist, paw; hind: hipHL/HR to knee, hock, paw). They start with a muscular thigh or upper-arm mass inside the torso (radius ~0.16 at the top, ~0.09 at the wrist), the hind legs with a slight backward hock bend. All indigo, with an indigoLight highlight sector down the front and a sumi outline stroke on the rear edge. Tiger paws: wide round indigo paw pads with 4 toe bumps each, ivory claws (small cones) pointing forward and slightly down, a thick cream fur cuff above each paw made of 5-6 small overlapping wedge tufts, plus a vermilion cuff band with a gold bead trim above it. A little wave motif (3 pale-blue arcs) on the outer side of each upper leg. Sumi paw pad lines. The paws rest flat on y=0 (lowest points at y≈0, sinking at most 0.02), with a front/hind pair at the same stance. Elbow and knee joints are marked by small indigoLight cap discs with a sumi ring. Everything stays chunky and simple, with flat colours.
parts.attaches: The leg tops sit inside the body torso at shoulderL/R and hipL/R. The legs ride the chest and pelvis chains.

parts.builds: The flame mane and the ox tail. Mane: a crest of broad, overlapping flame/wave-crest blades (extrudes, 2-3 rows) running from napeCrest over the neck and withers and along the spine to backCrestEnd, tallest (up to y~1.8) at the withers, shrinking toward the rump. The blades curl forward and up like Hokusai wave crests, ending in small curl hooks (spiral sweeps). The root-to-tip palette is stepped as hard bands, vermilionDark root, then vermilion, then gold, then cream tip, with a thin sumi outline plate under each blade and a base ridge of dark indigo. Shoulder and haunch kumo roundels: on each shoulder (±0.46, 1.1, 0.55) and each haunch (±0.46, 1.05, -0.72), a flat spiral cloud scroll (spiral sweeps with a gold disc centre and a vermilion ring, sumi outline) seated on the side of the body surface. Ox tail: a tapering indigo sweep on tail1..tail3 from tailRoot in an S that curls up to tailTip, with a sumi outline stroke, ending in a tuft of 7-9 flame blades fanned out (vermilion, gold, cream bands as in the mane) with 2-3 small curls. A few detached flame wisps (small flames) are rooted on the mane and tail only; nothing floats away from the body.
parts.attaches: The crest roots on the body's back line between napeCrest and backCrestEnd, behind the head box. Roundels sit on the body flanks at the shoulderL/R and hipL/R heights. The tail roots at tailRoot on the rump.

calls.reasoning:
I'm thinking through how to design a baku, the traditional dream-eating spirit, in ukiyo-e woodblock style—blending its mythic traits like an elephant trunk, rhino eyes, ox tail, tiger paws, and lion-like mane with swirling dream clouds reminiscent of classic wave motifs.

I'm now plotting precise proportions and coordinates for the creature: overall size around 1.3m wide, 1.9m tall, 2.9m long, with the body, legs, trunk, mane curls, and tail positioned along the z-axis to form a standing, forward-facing pose with a curled trunk and raised tail.

I'm sketching out the five main parts next, starting with the torso's distinctive tapir-style coloring—dark indigo at the front and rear with a cream saddle pattern in the middle using wave motifs—then the head with its jointed trunk, jaw, small fierce eyes, and ears.

Then I'm thinking through the legs with tiger-paw claws and fur cuffs, the flame-curl mane and tail with ornamental scrolls, and finally a dreamy floating wisp near the trunk tip with a glowing moon orb to suggest the baku inhaling dreams.

I'm keeping the dream-cloud wisp small, trailing from the trunk tip into the box boundaries, with the trunk hanging down-forward so the wisp curls near the nostril. Now I'm setting up the skeleton joints starting with the pelvis as root and building out the spine chain.

Defining joint positions and roles...

Finishing the tail chain with tail2 and tail3 joints, then moving to the leg hierarchy -- defining shoulderFL, elbowFL, and wristFL joint positions for the front-left leg with straight, tapir-like proportions rather than digitigrade bending.

Legs touch the ground at the paws near y=0. I'm picking a ukiyo-e inspired palette: deep indigo and prussian blue tones, paper cream, vermilion, sumi black, gold ochre, pale wave blue, sea green, beni pink, and a dreamy purple accent.

Now I'm mapping tapir body colors: indigo for head, neck, shoulders and forelegs; a cream saddle wrapping from shoulders to hips over the back and belly; indigo again for hindquarters and tail. The legs stay indigo with vermilion toe-cuff bands, gold claws, and a cream paw tuft touch. I'm also setting up joint mount points for the skeleton, like neck base, head base, and jaw positions.

Working through the trunk, ear, mane, and tail mount coordinates, then defining the body and head boxes with their joint assignments -- torso spans from pelvis up through chest with the saddle, spine ridge line, and hip/shoulder muscle swells, while the head box extends up to include the neck and jaw structure.

I'm settling on a six-part split: body, head (with neck, skull, jaw, ears, eyes, brows, tusks), trunk (bundled with the dream wisp), legs, mane (flame crest and shoulder scrolls), and tail (with the ox tuft), weighing whether to fold the small tail piece back into body instead.

Actually I'll simplify to five parts—body (torso, saddle with seigaiha pattern, tail), head, trunkDream, legs, and a combined maneTail that carries the flame-curl crest from neck down the back into the tail for a clean silhouette. Now I'm working out the bounding box coordinates so the head and trunk sections overlap correctly without gaps.

I also need the mane box to accommodate the curling tail, which rises from the pelvis up to around y 1.55, z -1.45, so I'm extending the mane box range to cover that span as well.

Checking overall proportions: total height comes to 1.8 with the mane peak and ear tips matching, so the silhouette reads correctly. The bounding size works out to roughly [1.3, 1.8, 3.4] once I account for the tail at the back and the trunk/wisp extending forward, with the width sitting around ±0.55 on x.

Allocating the triangle budget: body gets 150, head 200, trunk 120, legs 220, and the mane/tail 200, totaling 890 out of 900. Now I'm planning the ukiyo-e styling details for each part -- sumi-style dark outline sweeps, flat color fills, seigaiha wave-scale patterns on the saddle rendered as stacked concentric arcs in cream and blue, vermilion-and-gold cloud scroll motifs, and flame-like mane curls banded in vermilion to gold to cream to mimic woodblock bokashi shading.

I'm working out the body proportions next: torso radius around 0.42 wide and 0.4 tall at the chest, belly dropping to y=0.62, with the cream saddle patch spanning roughly z=-0.5 to 0.35 across the back and sides down toward the belly, edged with a scalloped wave-crest pattern in pale blue, while the indigo coloring covers the front to about z=0.35 and the hindquarters below z=-0.45. For the head, I'm sketching a tapir-like wedge skull with a domed forehead and small eyes featuring gold irises and sumi pupils, positioned symmetrically near the top of the face.

Now I'm pinning down skull dimensions and jaw placement, adding the trunk root, round cream-rimmed ears, and a pair of small ivory tusks flanking the trunk base to match the chimera's elephant-trunk, rhino-eye, ox-tail, tiger-paw blend -- and considering a small vermilion forehead emblem like a tomoe or teardrop mark as a finishing touch.

I'm also laying out kumadori-style vermilion cheek lines with ukiyo-e whiskers, segmenting the trunk into tapering tube sections with wrinkle rings and pink nostril detail, and sketching a trio of stacked cloud-swirl dream wisps with a tiny glowing moon and stars drifting from the trunk tip.

Now I'm working out the trunk joint chain positions and droop directions down to the tip mount, then setting up leg joint chains anchored to chest and pelvis with floor-level paw placement and forward-pointing claws, before organizing the full parts list—body, head with ears and jaw, and trunk segments—into their joint groupings.

For the mane and tail I'm designing a crest of overlapping flame-shaped blades with a vermilion-to-gold-to-cream gradient and sumi ink lines, curling like Hokusai wave crests, plus kumo-scroll roundel plates on the shoulders and haunches, and an ox-style tail ending in a curled flame tuft.

Now I'm plotting out the exact tail joint coordinates and directions to give it that S-curl shape, then compiling everything into the final JSON with all the mount points recorded.

I'm defining a buildTrunkDream function that sweeps a tapered trunk shape along a curved path using the three trunk joints, laying out control points from the root down to the tip.

Now I'm planning the surface details: color sectors for the belly versus base indigo, wrinkle rings as torus shapes placed along the sweep with radii decreasing toward the tip, a thin sumi stroke along the top, and a small vermilion lip ridge sweep, each bound to the nearest trunk bone based on position along the path.

For the tip, I'm adding a flared frustum cap oriented along the tangent direction, with two nostril discs (pink torus plus dark disc) positioned symmetrically on the downward-facing end.

Next I'm placing a small dream cloud off to the side of the trunk tip, around (0.2, 1.1, 1.75), using a box bounding region for puff spheres with darker outline accents, keeping it clear of the face area.

I'll add a ring outline that reads from both faces, then move to laying out the cloud clusters — three groups of four puffs each, plus a spiral tail sweep and a lilac dream ribbon curving from the cloud toward the nostril with a slight wobble.

Working through the ribbon's path points and checking where it lands near the nose tip, I need to lower the cloud cluster centers a bit so the ribbon connects more naturally to the underside near the nostril, then move on to building the moon's glow sphere.

Setting up the crescent shadow disc offset, scattering small glowing star octahedrons, and attaching the cloud bone to the trunk joint so it moves with the tip. Writing the aim-direction and tangent vector logic...

Still writing sweep geometry...

I need to write buildHead with Ctx, keeping it rich but concise and making sure the API calls are correct. I'm planning the neck sweep using a catmull path through the neck and head joints, binding the geometry to the bone chain for rigging.

For the skull I'm lofting a series of stations from the neck base up to the crown, with coordinates and widths/heights set for each station, bound to the head joint. Then I'm adding the jaw as a frustum box with its own bone binding, a small chin piece, a sumi line for the mouth, a pink tongue box, and small cone teeth, all positioned relative to the skull's bottom profile at each z-level. I'm also starting to place the eyes symmetrically based on the skull's width at that height.

Now I'm working out the eye construction using layered discs (sclera, iris, pupil slit, glint) positioned along an outward normal direction from the skull surface, built with a disc helper function using cylinder geometry, and then adding angled rod-based eyebrows positioned above each eye.

For the cheeks and forehead markings, I'm planning sweep curves draped onto the skull surface for cheek lines, and figuring out how to place the tomoe emblem by raycasting down onto the head surface to find the attachment point, then layering gold and vermilion disc elements there.

For ears, I'm positioning the joint and orienting the ear discs outward with their own normal direction, then layering concentric rings (sumi, indigo, cream, pink) with a small sphere tip, mirroring the setup for both left and right sides.

Now I'm sweeping bezier curves for the tusks with tapering radius and ivory color, adding fine whisker strokes from the muzzle with thin sumi rods, and building the neck as a catmull path with bones connecting the head joints, giving it an indigo fill and a thin sumi outline stroke along the top edge.

Next I'm adding a brow highlight using an indigo-colored flattened sphere stuck onto the skull's top surface, finding the right position with a surface ray cast to get the hit point before placing it.

For the muzzle, I'll leave the nostril-side front open without a cap and just add a tiny sumi dot for detail. I need to handle the Hit type as possibly null with a guard, and set up the ear rig using the earL bone for the left side with the appropriate sign convention, while importing catmull, bezier, and polyline utilities from the SDK.

I'm planning the body-building function, lofting between the pelvis, spine, and chest bones along the vertical axis with color bands assigned per segment.

Now I'm sketching out the station cross-sections from rump to chest, defining width, height, and vertical offset at each z-position so the body tapers naturally with a slight saddle dip in the back. I'm also working out the arc-length fractions for where the indigo-to-cream color transition should fall along the loft.

I'm setting up color bands for the body (indigo/cream/indigo) and a sector overlay for a shadowed belly patch, then planning a simpler ray-casting approach to place surface details by shooting rays inward from outside the body at given z-heights and angles.

Now I'm figuring out the scalloped edges along the front and rear saddle lines, looping points around the body at a fixed z and placing alternating cream/indigo wedge shapes—though I need to fix their orientation since the default cone placement sticks outward along the surface normal rather than along the edge direction.

Setting height, spacing, and alternating colors for the discs, then figuring out the seigaiha stacking pattern: rows and columns of overlapping circles per flank, each stack built from four shrinking discs in a cream/waveBlue/indigo sequence, adjusting since cream-on-cream would be invisible on that saddle.

I realize the part count is too high against the budget, so I'm cutting back to three discs per stack across fewer rows and columns to stay within limits.

Adding sumi lines, sash, bell, and tassels pushes the count toward 160, so I'm trimming back the seigaiha grid and stack counts to stay within budget—settling on 5 columns, 2-3 rows, and dropping the back stacks down to two. Then I'm planning the spine's sumi brushstroke as a curved sweep running along the top from back to front with a slight lift.

Now I'm sketching the sash as a vermilion loop around the mid-section, a gold knot sphere on the left flank with a smaller gold bell beneath it, and ivory tassel rods hanging down from the knot's attachment point.

I'm checking that the seigaiha wave pattern on the left side avoids overlapping the sash knot area around z=-0.05, y=0.8, which means shifting the row and column placements so the pattern doesn't collide with the sash loop.

For the haunch swirls, I'm figuring out how to generate sumi-style spiral arcs on the flank by computing points at growing radius around a center point on the surface, draping them along the curve.

I want two spirals per haunch at different centers so they don't overlap, each built from interpolated control points swept into a thin tube. For the hip bumps I'm planning small flattened indigo-light spheres embedded at the hip hit points to suggest bone structure underneath.

Now I'm wiring up the loft function with bone weights, bands, and sector parameters, passing in the actual joint objects for pelvis, spine, and chest. For the ring hits helper, I'm casting rays outward from a circle of angles around the body center to find surface collision points for placing the sweeps accurately.

I'm planning the buildManeTail function, using the existing tail joints to sweep a bone-weighted path across the chain for the tail geometry.

Since body surface points aren't reliably accessible, I decide to place things using explicit coordinates instead, mapping out the spine curve from the nape crest down through the back and neck base positions. For the mane crest blades, I'm working out a flame-shaped outline extruded along a forward-up plane, layered with stacked color bands (sumi base, dark vermilion, vermilion, gold, cream tip) to mimic a traditional crest design, and weighing simpler approaches to building those nested flame silhouettes without accidentally shrinking the base layer.

Writing flame outline logic...

Mapping blade heights and bone assignment by z-position for the mane, then realizing the three-row layout with full counts would blow past my 200-part budget, so I'm trimming the center row down to around 11 blades to stay within scope.

Working through the layered part budget—adding a dark base plate under each blade band and checking that layer thicknesses avoid z-fighting between the sumi base and the colored bands, while thinking through small curl-hook accents at the tips of center blades.

Now I'm designing the flank roundels: a sumi disc with a vermilion ring and gold center placed outward-facing on each side near the shoulder and haunch, plus a small spiral sweep accent built from cylinder and tube geometry oriented along the body's outward axis.

For the tail, I'm plotting a Catmull-Rom path through several joints to create a gentle S-curl from the root back and up, ending with a curved tip, then sweeping it with a tapered radius and indigo coloring along bone joints.

Now I'm adding a thin sumi stroke along that same tail path for outline detail, then designing a fan of eight flame-like blades at the tail tip, oriented in the yz-plane rotating from vertical to backward to form the tuft.

Totaling roughly 32 flame segments across 8 layers plus curls, with a bone tail sized around 3 units, and flame dimensions near 0.3 height by 0.07 width. I'm also adding small accent wisps near the mane crest tips, a few tiny single-band gold flames mixed into the side rows for extra detail.

Now I'm working out spiral curl hooks at the tips of the center blades, computing the tip position from the blade's height and curve offsets, then defining a spiral center and starting point so the hook curls forward and down convincingly.

I'm settling on the spiral radius, rotation axis, and turn count so the curl sweeps forward then dips, picking a gold tone for the tip accent. Then I move to mapping the spine path and blade orientation, deciding how to type the context object loosely rather than importing a formal type, and starting to assign color bands across the vertical range using vermilion variants.

Now I'm working out the flame shape's width function so it tapers naturally from base to tip, defining how the centerline bows forward and how each band's polygon is traced by sampling left and right edge points along the curve.

For the side rows (n≈11), I'm placing each blade at a point along the spine and computing its height from a bump profile centered near the withers, tallest around z≈0.45-0.5, tapering off toward the nape so the mane silhouette rises and falls naturally.

I'm clamping the center height so it stays within the bounding box, then scaling down the side rows and reworking the blade counts across sides, center, and tail along with hooks and roundels to keep the total element count manageable — trimming to roughly 8 blades per side row, 10 in the center, 7 tail blades times 4 parts, plus 6 hooks, 20 roundels, and a few ridge and tail elements.
